updateRules.single: Only one UPDATE per request. INSERT, DELETE, DDL and multiple statements separated by ";" are rejected.
updateRules.where: WHERE is required. To update every row, write WHERE true.
updateRules.returning: RETURNING is not supported — run a SELECT afterwards to check the result.
updateRules.limit: If more than 1000 rows change, everything is rolled back and an error is returned.
updateRules.tables: dev_* and databasechangelog* tables cannot be modified.
updateRules.timeout: Queries running longer than 30 seconds are cancelled.

usage.activeHint: Users with a request in the last 5 minutes

deps.title: Availability checks (every minute)
deps.hint: Pinged even without traffic, so you know a service is down before users hit it.

deployReport.title: This deploy vs the week before ({minutes} min running)

risks.hint: What will break, and when — and weak spots that hurt as data and traffic grow. Each risk says what will happen, the numbers behind it, what to do and where.
risks.none: No risks found. The detectors run every 15 minutes; long forecasts need about a week of history.
risks.acceptReason: Why is this acceptable? (shown to everyone)

startup.hint: What the last start did and how long it took: the slowest beans, SQL run at start, rows inserted, migrations.
startup.none: No startup was recorded (the panel records the start it was part of).
startup.everyStart: {table}: {rows} rows inserted at this start, and at earlier starts too

startup.ownRecorder: The application records startup steps itself, so bean timings are not available here.
startup.author: Author

advisor.title: Advisor
advisor.hint: Fixes PostgreSQL's own statistics point to: missing indexes, duplicates, cache candidates, outdated statistics, id limits. Refreshed every 6 hours.
advisor.cache: Cache candidates (read a lot, rarely changed)

profiler.hint: Samples what the application's threads run for a few seconds and draws a flame graph: the wider a block, the more time spent there. Purple is your code.
profiler.adminsOnly: Only admins can record a profile.
profiler.none: No profile yet. Record one while the slow thing happens.

runner.hint: Send a request to this application from the server itself (no proxy). Pick an endpoint: its parameters and body are filled in. The waterfall of the answer opens with one click.
runner.readOnly: Your account can view but not send requests.
runner.tokenNote: Paste a token of the application here; it is never stored by the panel.
runner.truncated: The answer is longer than 2 MB; only the start is shown.
runner.confirmWrite: {method} changes real data in production. Send it?

smoke.hint: Requests that must keep working. They run 2 minutes after every start and every 15 minutes; a failure turns Health red and alerts.
smoke.none: No smoke checks yet. Add the 3–5 requests users cannot live without.
smoke.name: Name
smoke.headersHint: One per line, Name: value. Use ${'{'}ENV_VARIABLE{'}'} for secrets so they stay out of the panel.

slo.hint: Goals per endpoint, e.g. "95% of calls within 500 ms". Shows whether each goal holds and when the month's allowance of slow calls runs out.
slo.none: No goals yet. Add one for the endpoints users wait for most.

tests.hint: Which endpoints the tests call, next to how production uses them. Write tests from the top of the list: busy, failing and untested first.
tests.how1: Run the tests once with the report written into the jar (works even if the deploy build skips tests), then commit the file:
tests.how2: Or upload target/devpanel-tests.json here. For line coverage, also upload target/site/jacoco/jacoco.csv.
tests.noCoverage: No JaCoCo report. Upload target/site/jacoco/jacoco.csv after mvn verify.

data.hint: Browse tables without writing SQL: filter, sort, page. Read-only.
data.none: Pick a table to see its rows.

panelAudit.hint: Everything done inside the panel: SQL run, queries stopped, log levels changed, accounts, requests sent, risks snoozed. Kept 180 days.

hints.cpu: Share of the processors used. Normal: under 70% most of the time. Above 90% for minutes, requests queue up; find the busy code with the Profiler.
hints.heap: Java's memory for objects. It rises and falls with garbage collection; what matters is the level right after GC (JVM tab). Constantly near the max means OutOfMemory is near.
hints.disk: How full each disk is. Above 90% plan cleanup: a full disk stops logs, uploads and often the database.
hints.pool: Database connections the application holds. Active = in use. If requests wait for a connection ("Waiting" above 0), slow queries or external calls inside transactions hold them too long.
hints.pending: Requests waiting for a free database connection right now. Should be 0.
hints.tomcat: Request threads in use out of the maximum. When all are busy, new requests queue and time out at the proxy.
hints.threadCount: Threads alive in the JVM. A count that only grows over days means something creates threads and never stops them.
hints.p95: 95% of calls were faster than this; 5% slower. Users feel p95 more than the average.
hints.timeSplit: Where an average call spends its time: database (blue), other services (orange), the application's own code (the rest).
hints.deadRows: Old row versions left by UPDATE/DELETE until vacuum cleans them. A few percent is normal; more than the live rows means vacuum falls behind.
hints.seqScans: How often PostgreSQL read the whole table. Fine for small tables; for big tables it usually means a missing index.
hints.indexScans: How often an index was used to find rows. Big tables should be read mostly this way.
hints.fkIndex: Without an index on the foreign key, finding the rows of one parent (and every delete of a parent) reads the whole table.
hints.gc: Garbage collections since start. Young: frequent and quick (a few ms) — normal. Full (Old Generation): stops the whole application; one now and then is fine, several per hour mean memory is short. Note: the heap histogram button forces one full GC.
hints.threadStates: What the threads are doing now. RUNNABLE: working or waiting on network. WAITING/TIMED_WAITING: idle, waiting for work. BLOCKED: waiting for a lock — should be 0.

state.RUNNABLE: Working on the CPU, or waiting for network/database (Java counts both as runnable)
state.WAITING: Idle, waiting for work (pool threads between tasks)
state.TIMED_WAITING: Sleeping with a timer (scheduled jobs, idle workers)
state.BLOCKED: Stuck waiting for a lock another thread holds — should be 0

hints.slo: A goal is met when, over 30 days, at least that share of calls answered within the target time.
hints.sloBurn: How fast the last 7 days spend the allowed slow calls: 1× is exactly on budget, above 1× the goal will be missed.
hints.trafficTested: Share of production calls that went to endpoints some test calls.
hints.startupTotal: From the JVM start until the application was ready to take requests.
hints.startupBeans: Own time: creating the bean itself (its constructor and {'@'}PostConstruct), without the beans it needed.
hints.profilerSelf: Itself: the method was on top of the stack (doing work itself). With calls: it was anywhere on the stack.
